title: Rotate a square matrix a quarter turn clockwise
summary: Turn a square floor of painted tiles a quarter turn clockwise in place: flip across the diagonal, then mirror each row.
goal: Turn the tile floor a quarter turn clockwise

mapping.story: Tile at row r, column c

examples.label: 3 × 3 floor
examples.explanation: The left column 1, 4, 7 becomes the top row, read upwards.

examples.label: 2 × 2 floor
examples.explanation: Each tile moves one corner clockwise.

examples.label: 1 × 1 floor
examples.explanation: A single tile looks the same.

ladder.name: Lay a new floor
ladder.idea: Build a new grid where the tile at (r, c) moves to (c, n − 1 − r), then copy it back.

ladder.name: Flip, then mirror
ladder.idea: Swap every tile with its partner across the main diagonal, then reverse each row. Both steps work in place.
ladder.insight: A quarter turn is the same as a transpose followed by a left-right mirror, and both of those are simple in-place swaps.

transfer.problem: Rotate a square image a quarter turn anticlockwise, in place.
transfer.explanation: Compose simple moves again: transpose, then reverse each column (or reverse each row first, then transpose).

selfCheck: Transposes by swapping only pairs above the diagonal.
